data.name: Mahakal
data.long_meaning: Mahakal refers to Shiva in his aspect as the lord of time. He is the destroyer of all things and is also responsible for the creation and preservation of the universe. This name signifies power, strength, and the passage of time.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the cyclical nature of time and the power to destroy and recreate.
data.numerology_meaning: People with this name are dynamic, resourceful, and adaptable. They are natural problem solvers and are always looking for new challenges to tackle.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mahakal holds great significance in Hindu culture as it symbolizes the power and authority of Lord Shiva, who is believed to rule over time and creation. Mahakal is also a commonly used name for Lord Shiva's temples and shrines.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Mahakal signifies the Lord's role as the destroyer of the universe at the end of each cosmic cycle. It also represents the cyclical nature of time and the impermanence of all things, reminding us of the transience of life and the importance of spiritual growth and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Mahakal, also known as Mahakaal or Mahadev, is the Hindu god of time and the god of death. He is often depicted as a meditating ascetic with multiple arms holding various symbols such as a trident, drum, and skull cup.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, around 1000 BCE to 500 CE
historical_references.context: Mahakal was an important deity in the Hindu pantheon during the Vedic and early Hindu periods. He was believed to be the sovereign lord of time and the ruler of the cremation grounds.

historical_references.reference: Mahakal is also revered as a destructive deity, Shiva, who represents the absolute ultimate reality and is responsible for the destruction of the universe in order to create a new one.
historical_references.time_period: Medieval India, around 600 CE to 1200 CE
historical_references.context: During the medieval Hindu period, Mahakal's destructive aspect as Shiva gained prominence. He was worshiped as the god of destruction and the bringer of new life.
